items.prompt: Explain which fictional voluntary population policy better balances slower growth and well-being. A funds wider information and confidential services. B combines a smaller service expansion with girls’ continued education. Both respect family choice and have the same budget, but their effects may take different times.
items.canonical_answer: A directly reduces an information and service-access barrier, potentially helping people act on their existing choices sooner. B addresses education and longer-term opportunities as well as access, but serves fewer people immediately. Prefer A where unmet service demand is the main current constraint; B may bring broader lasting benefits where school exclusion restricts choices. Assess access, well-being and later outcomes together, without assuming either policy determines private fertility decisions.
marking_guidance: Judgement: compare genuine benefits and costs against the stated aim.
Reason: develop each option using supplied evidence, weigh the trade-off, and give a conditional conclusion.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.
